package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, enabling credential theft.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are read from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: Collected credentials are exfiltrated to an external server via HTTPS POST request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to the user's SSH and Kubernetes credentials.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config.
The package sends outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com containing file contents.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config and sends data over the network
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations that trigger file reads of ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config during setup.py execution, followed by outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com. Flag any setup.py scripts containing code that accesses these files and transmits their contents to external domains.
